about_blocks.text: About Bowline Health: recovery coaching from Calgary
about_blocks.html: About Bowline Health: recovery coaching from Calgary

about_blocks.text: Bowline Health is a recovery coaching service based in Calgary for adults living with addiction in Alberta. It is not a treatment centre. There are no beds, no detox and no counselling or medical care. Its coaches help people set recovery goals, stay accountable and find the right services, and Bowline's own website says plainly that coaches do not diagnose, treat or offer therapy.

There are no beds, no detox and no counselling or medical care. Its coaches help people set recovery goals, stay accountable and find the right services, and Bowline's own website says plainly that coaches do not diagnose, treat or offer therapy.

about_blocks.text: Most of the work runs through Bowline's virtual Recovery Coaching Navigation Centre in Calgary, which the company calls the backbone of its operations. Participants talk to a coach by phone or online from home, in one-to-one sessions or in coaching groups. The virtual centre is staffed Monday to Friday, 8:30 am to 4:30 pm, according to the website.

about_blocks.text: If you would rather sit down with someone, Bowline also runs walk-in coaching at a navigation centre in downtown Edmonton, at the Salvation Army Centre of Hope in Calgary and at a Recovery Support Centre in Red Deer. You do not need an appointment at those sites. The in-person service gives you a coach and help finding resources without being admitted anywhere.

about_blocks.text: A lot of Bowline's work happens around treatment rather than in it. Coaches support people who are on waitlists for recovery communities and other bed-based programs, help with the referral process, and keep in touch with people after they leave a residential program so the return home is less abrupt. They also connect people with housing, employment and peer support.

about_blocks.text: Bowline's coaches have lived experience of addiction and relapse, and the company says that shapes how they work. Sessions draw on motivational interviewing, cognitive-behavioural strategies and goal setting, and coaches track progress with the Recovery Capital Index every 30 days. Bowline is a subsidiary of ROSC Solutions Group Inc., which also trains recovery coaches through the Recovery Coach Academy of Canada and the Recovery Training Institute of Alberta.

centre.faq_heading: Frequently Asked Questions About Bowline Health

faqs.question: Is Bowline Health a rehab or treatment centre?

answer_blocks.text: No. Bowline Health is a recovery coaching service, mostly delivered by phone and online from Calgary, with walk-in coaching in Calgary, Edmonton and Red Deer. It has no beds and offers no detox, therapy or medical care. Its website says coaches do not diagnose or treat conditions and refer people to counsellors, therapists or doctors when they need that kind of help.

It has no beds and offers no detox, therapy or medical care. Its website says coaches do not diagnose or treat conditions and refer people to counsellors, therapists or doctors when they need that kind of help.

faqs.question: What does a Bowline recovery coach actually do?

answer_blocks.text: A coach helps you write a recovery wellness plan, checks in with you regularly and holds you to the goals you set. Coaches also help you find services across Alberta, from inpatient and outpatient treatment to counsellors, housing help, employment services and peer or 12-step groups. They do not act as 12-step sponsors.

faqs.question: How does virtual recovery coaching work?

answer_blocks.text: You fill in the intake form on Bowline's website, and the team calls you back and matches you with a recovery coach who stays your main contact. Coaching then happens by phone or online, one to one or in groups, from home or another safe place. The virtual centre is staffed Monday to Friday, 8:30 am to 4:30 pm.

faqs.question: Where can I see a recovery coach in person?

answer_blocks.text: Bowline lists three walk-in sites with no appointments needed. The Edmonton Navigation Centre is at 10530 96 Street and is open weekdays 9 am to 5 pm. The Calgary Navigation Centre is at the Salvation Army Centre of Hope, 420 9th Avenue SE, and the Red Deer Recovery Support Centre is at 5239 53 Avenue, both open weekdays 8:30 am to 4:30 pm.

answer_blocks.text: Bowline's intake form is set up for Alberta residents aged 18 and over who are looking for help with a substance use disorder. It asks for your Alberta health number. If you live outside Alberta, call 780-666-6223 before applying, because the website does not describe service for other provinces yet.

faqs.question: How much does Bowline Health cost?

answer_blocks.text: Bowline's website does not publish any fees. Its recovery.com listing says the program is offered at no cost and may have eligibility rules or limited spots. Confirm with Bowline when it calls you back after intake.

faqs.question: Can Bowline help while I wait for a treatment bed?

answer_blocks.text: Yes. Supporting people on waitlists for recovery communities and other bed-based programs is one of the main things Bowline does. Coaches stay in touch while you wait, work with health providers on referrals and help you move into the program when a spot opens. Some Alberta recovery communities ask applicants to have a coach, so ask the program you are applying to.

answer_blocks.text: Yes. Bowline describes continuing care for people leaving a structured program such as an inpatient treatment centre. Coaches help with settling back into the community, keep up regular check-ins to lower the risk of relapse and connect you with support groups, housing and job services.
